subject: what happens when a user 'drops' a Shiny app in progress?

messages.author: 5117fd6c9c423ce1
messages.subject: what happens when a user 'drops' a Shiny app in progress?
parts:
Hi folks -

A Shiny app of mine is getting ready to go 'live' to several users.  I'm trying to understand what kind of traffic a Shiny server (not pro server) can handle,
and how to best manage it.  One question I have is, what exactly happens if, say, a session is started by a user and the user decides to abort the session
by closing the browser window, while Shiny is busy making a long calculation?  I assume the server 'figures it out' and releases any resources used by that
session, but that's just my assumption... do I need to be concerned about making sure my app cleans up after itself?

Related to that, since my app involves some relatively long calculations, I can anticipate my users thinking 'oh never mind, it's taking too long' and having a desire
for a ;'reset' button (vs having to start a whole new session).  In fact I have been asked for this feature.  Is there any simple way to build in that kind of capability in a Shiny app?

thank you.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: what happens when a user 'drops' a Shiny app in progress?
parts:
The answers are actually a little complicated.

If a user closes a window, then generally the current calculations executing on behalf of the user need to complete--we don't have a way to detect and abort the current calculations. The exception is if the useR leaving means there is nobody using that particular R process; then shiny server will wait a few seconds then ask the whole process to shut down.

There's no "never mind" button, no. I've never thought about it but that's interesting, I wonder whether it's even possible given how reactive programming works to interrupt a set of calculations and still have the world be in a consistent state. I'll think about it...
